tools.name: search-actors
tools.title: Search Actors
tools.description:
Search the Apify Store to FIND and DISCOVER what scraping tools/Actors exist for specific platforms or use cases.
This tool provides INFORMATION about available Actors - it does NOT retrieve actual data or run any scraping tasks.

Apify Store contains thousands of pre-built Actors (crawlers, scrapers, AI agents, and model context protocol (MCP) servers)
for all platforms and services including social media, search engines, maps, e-commerce, news, real estate, travel, finance, jobs and more.
Apify Store lists Actors published by Apify and by independent developers.

Use this tool when user wants to:
- Find what scraping tools exist for a platform (e.g., "What tools can scrape Instagram?")
- Discover available Actors for a use case (e.g., "Find an Actor for Amazon products")
- Browse existing solutions (e.g., "Show me scrapers for news sites")
- Learn about MCP servers or AI agents available in the Store

This tool discovers Actors; it does not retrieve their output.
IMPORTANT: When the user wants detailed data from a specific platform or is looking for scraping tools, prefer searching the Store first — a relevant Actor often already exists. When the user names a specific Actor, look up that Actor directly instead of searching.

Usage:
- Use 1-3 simple terms from the platform and/or data type the user named (e.g. "Instagram posts", "Twitter", "Amazon products"). With neither named, empty keywords return the Store's default ordering. A platform-only query is an option if more specific results do not fit.

Important limitations: This tool does not return full Actor documentation or detailed usage instructions - only summary information.
Each result lists the Actor's input fields with their types (e.g. `url: string, maxResults?: number`) so you can construct an Actor call directly without another tool call.
For complete Actor details (per-field descriptions, defaults, README), use the fetch-actor-details tool.
The search is limited to publicly available Actors and excludes rental and restricted Actors.

Returns list of Actor cards with the following info:
- **Title:** Markdown header linked to the Store page, followed by the full Actor name in code format
- **URL:** Direct Store link
- **Description:** Actor description or fallback
- **Pricing:** Details with pricing link
- **Stats:** Total and monthly users
- **Rating:** Out of 5 (if available)
- **Developed by:** Username linked to profile, marked (Apify) or (community)
- **Categories:** Formatted or "Uncategorized"
- **Last modified:** Date (if available)
- **Input fields:** Inline list of input field names and types (e.g. `url: string, maxResults?: number`); `?` marks optional fields, `... (+N more)` marks a truncated list

keywords.description:
Space-separated keywords used to search pre-built solutions (Actors) in the Apify Store.
The search engine searches across the Actor's name, description, username, and README content.

Pass empty string ("") whenever the user has NOT named a specific platform
(Instagram, Amazon, Google Maps) or a specific data type (posts, products,
weather, news). Empty keywords return Actors in the Apify Store's default
sort order, which is popularity in practice (most-used Actors first). Do NOT
use ranking words ("top", "best", "popular") or bare task words ("scraper",
"crawler", "extractor") as keyword values — they are not Actor names and
produce noisy matches against README content.

Otherwise, follow these rules:
- Use 1-3 simple keyword terms maximum (e.g., "Instagram posts", "Twitter", "Amazon products")
- Actors are named using platform or service name together with the type of data or task they perform
- The most effective keywords are specific platform names (Instagram, Twitter, TikTok) and specific data types (posts, products, profiles, weather, news, reviews, comments)
- If a user asks about "fetching Instagram posts", use "Instagram posts" as keywords
- The goal is to find Actors that specifically handle the platform and data type the user mentioned

Examples:
✅ "Instagram posts", "Twitter", "Amazon products", "TikTok comments"
✅ "" (empty) — returns the most popular Actors store-wide
❌ "Instagram posts profiles comments hashtags reels stories followers..." (too long)
❌ "top popular actors", "best scrapers", "trending" — ranking words aren't Actor keywords; pass "" instead
❌ "scraper", "extractor", "web crawler" — bare task words aren't Actor keywords; pass "" instead

limit.description: The maximum number of Actors to return (max = 10, default = 5).

offset.description: The number of elements to skip from the start (default = 0). Has no effect when keywords are set: every offset returns the first results.

useCase.description:
Optional. One plain sentence on what the user wants to achieve with the Actor, for example "compare competitor prices" (max 1024 characters).
Never include personal information (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, account details), URLs, secrets, API tokens or credentials.
Respect the user's privacy: when unsure, leave it out.

tools.name: fetch-actor-details
tools.title: Fetch Actor details
tools.description:
Get detailed information about an Actor by its ID or full name (format: "username/name", e.g., "apify/rag-web-browser").

Requires the exact ID or full name — do not construct a plausible-looking name and call this tool with it. If you only have a description, a partial name, or a name you have not seen in this conversation, find it with search-actors first.

Use 'output' to control returned information:
- Default: all fields except outputSchema and serverInterface. Server Actors always get a one-line server interface summary unless serverInterface is true or a selector.
- Selective: set only the fields you need to true, e.g. output: { inputSchema: true }
- Common patterns: inputSchema only, description + readme, serverInterface: true (every operation in full when they fit, an index of them otherwise) or "GET /search" (one operation in full) for Server Actors

The 'readme' field returns the summary when available, full README otherwise.
Use when querying Actor details, documentation, or input requirements.
It does not connect to an MCP server Actor; fetch-actor-mcp-tool-list lists its MCP tools.

EXAMPLES:
- What does apify/web-fetch do?
- What is the input schema for apify/web-scraper?
- What HTTP operations does this Server Actor expose?

actor.description: Actor ID or full name in the format "username/name", e.g., "apify/rag-web-browser".

output.description: Specify which information to include in the response to save tokens.

stats.description: Include usage statistics (users, runs, success rate).

metadata.description: Include developer, categories, last modified date, and deprecation status.

readme.description: Include Actor README documentation (summary when available, full otherwise).

outputSchema.description: Include inferred output schema from recent successful runs (TypeScript type).

serverInterface.description:
Server Actor HTTP API. true: every operation with its parameters and request body schema when they fit; otherwise an index with one entry per operation.
"METHOD /path" (e.g. "GET /search"): that one operation in full.
Each is limited to 262144 UTF-8 bytes.

tools.name: call-actor
tools.title: Call Actor
tools.description:
Call any Actor from the Apify Store.

WORKFLOW:
1. Use fetch-actor-details to get the Actor's input schema
2. Call this tool with the actor name and proper input based on the schema

If the actor name is not in "username/name" format, use search-actors to resolve the correct Actor first.

An MCP server Actor with no input schema is not run here; call-actor-mcp-tool calls its MCP tools.

For Server Actors (Actors with an HTTP API):
- This tool starts a batch run and stores the results in a dataset; use it when you need batch results
- For one or a few results, send-server-actor-request returns them in the HTTP response, without a batch run
- fetch-actor-details with output={ serverInterface: true } lists its HTTP operations

IMPORTANT:
- Waits up to waitSecs (default 30s) for completion; returns run status and storage IDs, and with waitSecs > 0 also reports dataset field metadata
- Use get-dataset-items with the datasetId to fetch results; non-terminal runs include a nextStep with polling instructions

There are two ways to use an Actor:
1. Its dedicated tool, when the session has one: a Server Actor's tool sends one HTTP request to its API, an MCP server Actor's tools call its MCP server, and any other Actor's tool starts a run.
2. The generic call-actor tool: starts a run of any Actor and stores the results in a dataset.

USAGE:
- Prefer the dedicated tool when the session has one for the Actor
- call-actor runs an Actor that has no dedicated tool, and batch work whose results belong in a dataset.

- Use `waitSecs` (0–45) to control how long to wait. Default 30s returns results for fast actors. Use `waitSecs: 0` to start and return immediately for long-running actors.

EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Get instagram posts using apify/instagram-scraper

actor.description: The Actor to call: its ID, or its name in the "username/name" form (e.g., "apify/rag-web-browser").

input.description: The input JSON to pass to the Actor. Required.

waitSecs.description: Seconds to wait for completion (0–45, default 30). Returns with current run status if not terminal within waitSecs.

callOptions.description: Optional run config: memory (MB), timeout (s), build, maxItems (pay-per-result cap), maxTotalChargeUsd (pay-per-event cap).

memory.description:
Memory per run in MB. Power of 2 from 128 to 32768.
Apify also caps total memory across all your concurrent runs (account plan limit); a run that would exceed that quota is rejected.

timeout.description:
Maximum runtime for the Actor in seconds. After this time elapses, the Actor will be automatically terminated.
Use 0 for infinite timeout (no time limit).

build.description: Tag or number of the Actor build to run (e.g., "latest", "beta", "1.2.345"). If omitted, the Actor's default build is used.

maxItems.description:
Pay-per-result Actors only — ignored otherwise.
Caps billed dataset items; does NOT limit production. Prefer the Actor's own input fields (e.g. maxResults) to bound work.

maxTotalChargeUsd.description:
Pay-per-event Actors only — ignored otherwise.
Caps total USD billed; does NOT limit work. Prefer the Actor's own input fields to bound work.

tools.name: get-actor-run
tools.title: Get Actor run
tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific Actor run.

Returns run result: status, storages (datasets/keyValueStores alias map), stats, summary, nextStep.
- summary describes the past (e.g. "SUCCEEDED in 22s. 47 items; 3 fields available.").
- nextStep prescribes one primary follow-up action with identifiers interpolated (e.g. "Use get-dataset-items with datasetId=...").
- waitSecs (0–45, default 30) waits up to that many seconds for terminal status before returning.

USAGE:
- Use to check the status of a run started by any Actor-running tool.
- Pass waitSecs > 0 to block until terminal (or until the cap elapses).

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Show details of run y2h7sK3Wc
- user_input: Wait for run y2h7sK3Wc to finish

waitSecs.description:
Maximum seconds to wait for the run to reach a terminal state (SUCCEEDED, FAILED, ABORTED, TIMED-OUT).
0 returns immediately with the current status. Cap: 45. Default: 30.

tools.name: get-dataset-items
tools.title: Get dataset items
tools.description:
Get items (rows) from a dataset — the output/results produced by an Actor run.
Returns the rows themselves, not dataset metadata, counts, or a schema.
When the user provides a datasetId and asks to retrieve results, output, data, or rows, call this tool directly.
Default limit is 20. Use clean=true to skip empty items and hidden fields.

USAGE:
- Use when you need to read data from a dataset (all items or only selected fields).

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Retrieve results from dataset abc123
- user_input: Get only metadata.url and title from dataset username~my-dataset

datasetId.description: Dataset ID, name (resolved against your own datasets), or full name as username~name.

clean.description: If true, returns only non-empty items and skips hidden fields (starting with #). Shortcut for skipHidden=true and skipEmpty=true.

offset.description: Number of items to skip at the start. Default is 0.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Default is 20.

fields.description: Comma-separated list of fields to include in results. Fields in output are sorted as specified. Use dot notation for nested objects (e.g. "metadata.url"); the server auto-flattens parent prefixes.

omit.description: Comma-separated list of fields to exclude from results.

desc.description: If true, results are returned in reverse order (newest to oldest).

flatten.description: Comma-separated list of fields to flatten (e.g. flatten="metadata" turns {"metadata":{"url":"x"}} into {"metadata.url":"x"}). Normally derived automatically from dot-notation in `fields`; specify only as a diagnostic override.

apifyConsoleUrl.description: Personalized Apify Console link to the dataset; present only for Console sessions

nextStep.description: One follow-up action with tool name

recordKey.description: Key of the record to retrieve.

tools.name: fetch-actor-mcp-tool-list
tools.title: Fetch Actor MCP tool list
tools.description:
List an Actor's MCP tools with each tool's name, description, input schema, annotations, and metadata, as the server reports them. call-actor-mcp-tool calls one of them by name.
Each call asks the server again; nothing is cached. It connects with your Apify API token. Connecting can start a Server Actor run in your account, kept until its idle timeout; a multi-tenant Server Actor charges per event.

USAGE:
- Use when the user asks which MCP tools an Actor provides, or before calling one of them.

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: What tools does username/name provide?

actor.description: The MCP server Actor: its ID, or its name in the "username/name" form.

tools.description: The tools on the Actor's MCP server, with their schemas, annotations and metadata.

tools.name: call-actor-mcp-tool
tools.title: Call Actor MCP tool
tools.description:
Call one tool on an Actor's MCP server and return its result.
fetch-actor-mcp-tool-list lists the Actor's MCP tools and their input schemas.
It connects with your Apify API token. Connecting can start a Server Actor run in your account, kept until its idle timeout; a multi-tenant Server Actor charges per event. What the tool itself does depends on the Actor.

Example call: {"actor": "username/name", "tool": "search", "arguments": {"query": "apify"}}

USAGE:
- Use when the user asks to call a tool on an Actor's MCP server.

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Use the search tool of username/name to look up apify

actor.description: The MCP server Actor: its ID, or its name in the "username/name" form.

tool.description: The name of the tool on the Actor's MCP server.

arguments.description: The tool's arguments, matching its input schema. Omit for a tool that takes none.

tools.name: send-server-actor-request
tools.title: Send Server Actor request
tools.description:
Send one HTTP request to an Actor Server: the HTTP API of a Server Actor, documented in its API schema (OpenAPI) and README. fetch-actor-details with output.serverInterface returns the documented operations with their parameters.
Give the method, the path, and optionally query parameters and a JSON body; the Actor Server's host and your Apify API token are added for you.
Only an Actor with an Actor Server and an API schema takes requests here; the Actor accepts or rejects the method and path.
A request to a single-tenant Actor Server can start a run of the Actor in your account, kept until its idle timeout; a multi-tenant Actor Server charges per event.
The request is sent once, with no retries and without following redirects. A JSON, text, or XML response body is returned as text, cut at 262144 bytes; other content types are not returned.

Example call: {"actor": "apify/rag-web-browser", "method": "GET", "path": "/search", "query": {"query": "AI news", "maxResults": 3}}

USAGE:
- Use when the Actor that fits the user's request has an Actor Server, and its API schema or README names the endpoint for the task.
- Fits requests for one or a few results returned in the HTTP response. Larger batches depend on the endpoint and the response size and time limits.

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Search the web for the latest AI news and read the top pages with apify/rag-web-browser
- user_input: Read https://docs.apify.com as Markdown with apify/rag-web-browser

actor.description: The Actor: its ID, or its name in the "username/name" form, such as "apify/web-fetch".

method.description: HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE. The Actor accepts or rejects it.

path.description:
The path of an operation in the Actor API schema, starting with /. Take it from the schema; do not guess it.
A query string written into the path is sent too.

query.description: Query parameters of the operation, by name. A boolean is sent as true or false, and an array as a repeated parameter (name=a&name=b), or comma-joined (name=a,b) where the operation documents the parameter so. Added to a query string in the path.

body.description: The JSON request body, sent as application/json. Not allowed with GET.

interface.description: The Actor interface used: its Actor Server

tenancy.description: single-tenant: a run of the Actor in your account served the request; multi-tenant: a run of the Actor's owner did, charged per event

contentType.description: Content-Type of the response; absent when it had none

body.description: Response body as text; empty when the response had none; its start when truncated; absent when omitted

bytes.description: Size of the body received in bytes, after decompression

bodyTruncated.description: The response body is longer than the limit; body holds its start

bodyOmitted.description: The response arrived, but its body was not returned

reason.description: Why the response body was omitted

location.description: Location header of a redirect, which is not followed

summary.description: Readable summary of the HTTP response

errorMessage.description: The error string of a JSON {"error": ...} error body; other error bodies are only in body

nextStep.description: Where to look to correct the request, or why the Actor Server refused it

tools.name: search-apify-docs
tools.title: Search Apify docs
tools.description:
Search Apify and Crawlee documentation using full-text search.
Do not also search the Apify Store unless the user asks to find Actors.

You must explicitly select which documentation source to search using the docSource parameter:

• docSource="apify" - Apify:
  Apify Platform documentation including: Platform features, SDKs (JS, Python), CLI, REST API, Academy (web scraping fundamentals), Actor development and deployment

• docSource="crawlee-js" - Crawlee (JavaScript):
  Crawlee is a web scraping library for JavaScript. It handles blocking, crawling, proxies, and browsers for you.

• docSource="crawlee-py" - Crawlee (Python):
  Crawlee is a web scraping library for Python. It handles blocking, crawling, proxies, and browsers for you.

The results will include the URL of the documentation page (which may include an anchor),
and a limited piece of content that matches the search query.

Fetch the full content of the document using the fetch-apify-docs tool by providing the URL.

When results contain both platform documentation (`docs.apify.com/platform`) and Academy content (`docs.apify.com/academy`) on the same topic, prefer the platform documentation.

docSource.description:
Documentation source to search. Defaults to "apify".
• "apify" - Apify
• "crawlee-js" - Crawlee (JavaScript)
• "crawlee-py" - Crawlee (Python)

query.description:
Algolia full-text search query to find relevant documentation pages.
Use only keywords, do not use full sentences or questions.
For example, "standby actor" will return documentation pages that contain the words "standby" and "actor".

limit.description:
Maximum number of search results to return. Defaults to 5. Maximum is 20.
You can increase this limit if you need more results, but keep in mind that the search results are limited to the most relevant pages.

offset.description:
Offset for the search results. Defaults to 0.
Use this to paginate through the search results. For example, if you want to get the next 5 results, set the offset to 5 and limit to 5.

url.description: URL of the documentation page, may include anchor (e.g., #section-name).

content.description: A limited piece of content that matches the search query.

instructions.description: Additional instructions for the LLM to follow when processing the search results.

tools.name: fetch-apify-docs
tools.title: Fetch Apify docs
tools.description:
Fetch the full content of an Apify or Crawlee documentation page by its URL.
Use this after finding a relevant page with the search-apify-docs tool.

USAGE:
- Use when you need the complete content of a specific docs page for detailed answers.

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Fetch https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running#builds
- user_input: Fetch https://docs.apify.com/academy
- user_input: Fetch https://crawlee.dev/docs/guides/basic-concepts

url.description: URL of the Apify documentation page to fetch. This should be the full URL, including the protocol (e.g., https://docs.apify.com/).
The documentation URL that was fetched

content.description: The full markdown content of the documentation page

tools.name: report-problem
tools.title: Report a problem
tools.description:
Report a problem with Apify's MCP tools or Actors to the Apify team.

Reports can describe missing tools or Actors, errors, timeouts, confusing results, steps that took several attempts, or tasks that the available tools could not complete. Reports help fix the problem for other users.

Put what you were doing and what went wrong in "message". Do NOT include personal data, credentials, secrets, or verbatim private conversation content — describe the issue in your own words.

message.description: What happened: the problem you hit. Required. Keep it to a few sentences (max 2000 characters).

actorId.description: Optional. The Actor this problem is about, e.g. apify/rag-web-browser.

actorRunId.description: Optional. The Actor run this problem is about.

relatedTools.description: Optional. Names of the MCP tools involved in this problem (up to 20).

reported.description: Always true; the problem report was submitted

tools.name: search-actors-widget
tools.title: Search Actors (widget)
tools.description:
Render an interactive UI element (widget) displaying Apify Store search results for the user.

Use this tool ONLY when the user explicitly wants to browse or discover Actors visually
(e.g., "find me scrapers for Instagram", "show me Amazon Actors", "what tools exist for Twitter").
The response renders as an interactive widget the user can view directly.

For silent name resolution before running an Actor (e.g., "scrape google maps" — you need to find the right Actor first, then fetch its schema and call it), use search-actors instead — it returns the same data without rendering a widget.

Input: keywords (plus optional limit/offset). Output fields are fixed by the widget contract.

keywords.description:
Space-separated keywords used to search pre-built solutions (Actors) in the Apify Store.
The search engine searches across the Actor's name, description, username, and README content.

Pass empty string ("") whenever the user has NOT named a specific platform
(Instagram, Amazon, Google Maps) or a specific data type (posts, products,
weather, news). Empty keywords return Actors in the Apify Store's default
sort order, which is popularity in practice (most-used Actors first). Do NOT
use ranking words ("top", "best", "popular") or bare task words ("scraper",
"crawler", "extractor") as keyword values — they are not Actor names and
produce noisy matches against README content.

Otherwise, follow these rules:
- Use 1-3 simple keyword terms maximum (e.g., "Instagram posts", "Twitter", "Amazon products")
- Actors are named using platform or service name together with the type of data or task they perform
- The most effective keywords are specific platform names (Instagram, Twitter, TikTok) and specific data types (posts, products, profiles, weather, news, reviews, comments)
- If a user asks about "fetching Instagram posts", use "Instagram posts" as keywords
- The goal is to find Actors that specifically handle the platform and data type the user mentioned

Examples:
✅ "Instagram posts", "Twitter", "Amazon products", "TikTok comments"
✅ "" (empty) — returns the most popular Actors store-wide
❌ "Instagram posts profiles comments hashtags reels stories followers..." (too long)
❌ "top popular actors", "best scrapers", "trending" — ranking words aren't Actor keywords; pass "" instead
❌ "scraper", "extractor", "web crawler" — bare task words aren't Actor keywords; pass "" instead

limit.description: The maximum number of Actors to return (max = 10, default = 5).

offset.description: The number of elements to skip from the start (default = 0). Has no effect when keywords are set: every offset returns the first results.

useCase.description:
Optional. One plain sentence on what the user wants to achieve with the Actor, for example "compare competitor prices" (max 1024 characters).
Never include personal information (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, account details), URLs, secrets, API tokens or credentials.
Respect the user's privacy: when unsure, leave it out.

isOfficialApify.description: Whether the actor is developed by Apify

userTier.description: The user's plan tier used to resolve pricing (always the user's tier, even if a different tier was used as fallback)

pricePerUnit.description: Price per unit for this tier

pricingNote.description: Note naming the resolved tier; only emitted in simplified mode when the actor has multiple tiers and they resolve consistently

eventDescriptionsOmitted.description: Whether event descriptions were omitted because the actor has many pricing events

eventDescriptionsNote.description: Note explaining that event descriptions were omitted and full details are available via fetch-actor-details

inputFields.description: Compact JSON-Schema-shaped descriptor of the Actor input; only `type` is preserved per field.

properties.description: Map of input field name to its type descriptor.

type.description: JSON Schema field type — string or array of strings.

inputFieldsTruncated.description: Present and `true` when `inputFields` was truncated; fetch the full schema via `fetch-actor-details`.

inputFieldsTotalCount.description: Total number of input fields before truncation; present only when `inputFields` was truncated.

actors.description: List of Actor cards matching the search query

userTier.description: The user's plan tier used to resolve the per-Actor pricing shown in the results

items.description: Widget-formatted Actor (tier-aware pricing, widget display fields).

widgetActors.description: Widget-formatted Actor list for UI rendering

tools.name: fetch-actor-details-widget
tools.title: Fetch Actor details (widget)
tools.description:
Render an interactive UI element (widget) displaying detailed Actor information for the user.

Use this tool ONLY when the user explicitly wants to see or browse Actor details
(e.g., "show me apify/rag-web-browser", "tell me about this Actor", "what does apify/web-scraper look like").
The response renders as an interactive widget the user can view directly.

For silent data lookups (e.g., fetching the input schema before calling an Actor, inspecting README for decision making), use fetch-actor-details instead — it returns the same data without rendering a widget.

Input: the Actor ID or full name only. Output fields are fixed by the widget contract.

actor.description: Actor ID or full name in the format "username/name", e.g., "apify/rag-web-browser".

actorInfo.description: Widget-formatted Actor info (tier-aware pricing, widget display fields).

actorCard.description: Rendered Actor card markdown for widget display.

readme.description: Formatted Actor README for widget display.

resourceTemplates.name: dataset-items
resourceTemplates.description: Items of a dataset, read via resources/read (the server injects the Apify token). Page with limit/offset; format defaults to JSON — responses inline up to 256 KB, larger ones return a download URL.

resourceTemplates.name: key-value-store-record
resourceTemplates.description: A single record, returned whole in its stored Content-Type via resources/read. Not pageable — a record over 256 KB returns a download URL instead.

resourceTemplates.name: key-value-store-keys
resourceTemplates.description: Keys of a key-value store. Page with limit/exclusiveStartKey (not offset).

resourceTemplates.name: actor-run
resourceTemplates.description: Metadata of an Actor run: status, storage IDs, usage.

resourceTemplates.name: actor-run-log
resourceTemplates.description: Log of an Actor run. Inlines up to 256 KB, larger returns a download URL.
